startup.name: Invertix
startup.one_liner: AI agents that operate energy plants and datacenters
startup.description:
Invertix builds AI that helps energy companies run Power Plants Autonomously.
We believe Power Plants and Datacenters will be autonomously developed and operated.
We are building that AI layer.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0uDH6pMn5OE

Critical Infrastructure is a $10 trillion market.

yc_acceptance.basis: Starting rate is about 1 percent with a 0.6 to 2 percent band. The company is already accepted, so this is a note only. A team of 8 in San Francisco on AI for energy and datacenters matches a hot theme, but the description gives little about customers or founders, which holds the estimate near the low end.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because the pitch is a vision of autonomous power plants with a trillion dollar market claim and no evidence of customers or pilots. Utilities and plant owners move slowly and are risk averse, so reviewers would ask how a startup gets control access to real plants.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most stall because sales cycles are long, plants are conservative and incumbents bundle software. Acquisition by an energy software company under 100M, like glow energy, is the most common good result.

killers.risk: Plant owners will not grant autonomous control
killers.evidence: Power plants are safety critical and regulated, and buyers favor advisory tools over autonomy.
killers.mitigation: Start with advisory mode and earn control on one asset class.

killers.risk: Slow sales cycles starve the company of revenue
killers.evidence: Energy analogs raised only small rounds or took years to reach A.
killers.mitigation: Target independent power producers and datacenters with faster decisions.

killers.risk: Incumbents and OEMs bundle AI into their control systems
killers.evidence: Inverter and SCADA vendors already own the plant data and control interfaces.

killers.risk: Vision is broad and the team spreads thin
killers.evidence: The pitch covers plants and datacenters across all of critical infrastructure.
killers.mitigation: Pick one asset class, such as solar plus storage.

competition_now.name: Emerald AI
competition_now.what: Software that makes data centers flexible grid assets.
competition_now.traction: Raised a 24.5M seed and later rounds, with Nvidia backing.

competition_now.name: GridCARE
competition_now.what: Frees idle grid power for AI datacenters.

technical_complexity.rationale: Autonomous control of real plants needs reliable models, integration with proprietary SCADA and inverter systems, safety validation and regulatory acceptance. A team of 8 can build advisory and optimization, but earning control authority takes long pilots.

takeover_risk.rationale: Incumbents own the data and customer relationships, but moving to autonomy is slow for them. Well funded datacenter power startups could extend into plant operations.

evidence.claim: Datacenter power and grid software is attracting large rounds, such as Emerald AI and GridCARE.
AI datacenters face multi year interconnection queues, which creates demand for software.

actions: Sign one letter of intent with an operator
Demo control in simulation with real data
Run advisory mode on three plants

roadmap.goal: Move to paid multi site contracts.

pros.evidence: AI datacenter power demand drives many funded startups in adjacent niches.
A larger team than typical suggests an existing product effort.

brand.rationale: An ix suffix coinage hints at inverters, helpful for solar buyers but narrow if the company expands to datacenters. Suffix coinages are common in earlier YC cohorts and neutral to outcomes.

narrative.headline: An ambitious AI for power plant operations pitch with a decent chance of a seed and long, slow later steps.
narrative.general_summary: Invertix builds AI to operate power plants and datacenters autonomously. The theme is hot, with large rounds for neighbors like Emerald AI and GridCARE. But the pitch is broad, the description lacks customers, sales cycles are long, and plant owners are cautious about autonomy. A seed above the YC deal is likely but not certain, and the energy analogs show few Series A rounds, with raptor maps the one that went the distance after a pivot.

assumptions: Blind test: only the batch input file was used for the company.
A seed here means a round above the YC deal of about 500K within about 12 months of the batch start.
Industrials cohorts have under 30 companies, so rates are anecdotes.
Market search results dated before 2026-10-05 were used.
